dependency_or_rule_change: K-pop export visibility depends in part on foreign-owned chart systems and foreign-controlled stream or sales weighting rules.
safe_econ_reading: The cleanest baseline reading is foreign metric dependence in export-facing scoreboards, not automatic proof of Korean average-industry discrimination.
main_limit_or_counterevidence: Any export-oriented non-U.S. music industry can face similar scoreboard dependence, so this baseline is not uniquely Korean without comparative evidence.

dependency_or_rule_change: Weekly digital-download counting tightened from four to one per customer per week.
safe_econ_reading: This is best read as a disproportionate hit to repeat-download-heavy fandom strategies rather than direct anti-K-pop intent.
main_limit_or_counterevidence: The available source record supports a broad anti-manipulation interpretation and does not show the rule was written specifically for K-pop.

dependency_or_rule_change: A low-price floor for album and EP sales counting reduced the usefulness of steeply discounted fan-purchase campaigns.
safe_econ_reading: The strongest economic reading is that foreign-owned chart rules can reduce the payoff to fandom-driven purchase strategies that some K-pop releases used heavily.
main_limit_or_counterevidence: This still looks more like a general anti-dumping or anti-manipulation adjustment than a Korea-targeted design choice.

dependency_or_rule_change: Hot 100 methodology excludes digital singles sold through direct-to-consumer artist stores from chart calculations.
safe_econ_reading: This row captures dependence on foreign scoreboard methodology because chart success depends on which retailer channels the foreign-owned system recognizes as valid.
main_limit_or_counterevidence: The row weakens direct fan-purchase channels but does not by itself imply anti-K-pop purpose or an industry-wide Korean revenue shock.

dependency_or_rule_change: Global chart methodology weights subscription and ad-supported official streams plus official retailer sales inside the Billboard-Luminate system.
safe_econ_reading: The cleanest reading is metric dependence: export-facing chart outcomes are partly functions of a foreign-owned weighting system for monetized streams and official sales.
main_limit_or_counterevidence: This row points to dependency on foreign formula design, not direct proof that Korean acts are singled out relative to all other non-U.S. acts.

dependency_or_rule_change: YouTube data stopped being delivered to U.S. Billboard charts after a weighting dispute between YouTube and Billboard.
safe_econ_reading: This shows that export-facing chart visibility can be affected by bargaining between foreign platform and foreign scoreboard owners, which reinforces metric dependence.
main_limit_or_counterevidence: The current record frames the event as a platform-to-platform weighting dispute rather than a Korea-specific penalty, so it should not be overread as anti-K-pop evidence.

dependency_or_rule_change: Melon and FLO were added to the Luminate Republic of Korea streaming panel during 2023.
safe_econ_reading: This is explicit counterevidence to a blanket exclusion story because Korean domestic streaming data became more visible inside the foreign-owned measurement system.
main_limit_or_counterevidence: The inclusion improves representation but does not remove foreign control of scoreboard design or make the issue industry-wide by itself.
